We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

|  | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $3$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $-3$ |
|  | $↓$ | $3$ | $6$ | $24$ |
|  | $1$ | $2$ | $8$ | $21$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+2x-3}{x-3}={x}^{2}+2x+8+\frac{21}{x-3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+2x-3}{x-3}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+2x+8+\frac{21}{x-3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x+8{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x+21{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+8x\,{|}_{0}^{1}+21\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({1}^{3}-{0}^{3})+({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})+8(1-0)+21(\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-3|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0-3|) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+1+8+21(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =\frac{28}{3}+21\operatorname{ln}⁡(\,\frac{2}{3}\,).\end{aligned}
$$
